In [[geometry]], a '''prismatic compound of antiprism''' is a category of [[uniform polyhedron compound]]. Each member of this infinite family of uniform polyhedron compounds is a symmetric arrangement of [[antiprism]]s sharing a common axis of rotational symmetry.

== Infinite family ==
This infinite family can be enumerated as follows:
*For each positive integer ''n'' ≥ 1 and for each rational number ''p''/''q'' > 3/2 (expressed with ''p'' and ''q'' [[coprime]]), there occurs the compound of ''n'' ''p''/''q''-gonal antiprisms, with symmetry group:
**'''D<sub>''np''d</sub>''' if ''nq'' is odd
**'''D<sub>''np''h</sub>''' if ''nq'' is even

When ''p''/''q'' = 2, or equivalently p = 2, q = 1, the component is the [[tetrahedron]] (or dyadic antiprism). In this case, if ''n'' = 2 then the compound is the [[stella octangula]], with higher symmetry ('''O<sub>h</sub>''').

== Compounds of two antiprisms ==
Compounds of two ''n''-antiprisms share their vertices with a 2''n''-[[prism (geometry)|prism]], and exist as two [[alternation (geometry)|alternated]] set of vertices.

[[Cartesian coordinates]] for the vertices of an antiprism with ''n''-gonal bases and isosceles triangles are
*<math>\left( \cos\frac{k\pi}{n}, \sin\frac{k\pi}{n}, (-1)^k h \right)</math>
*<math>\left( \cos\frac{k\pi}{n}, \sin\frac{k\pi}{n}, (-1)^{k+1} h \right)</math>

with ''k'' ranging from 0 to 2''n''−1; if the triangles are equilateral,
:<math>2h^2=\cos\frac{\pi}{n}-\cos\frac{2\pi}{n}.</math>

=== Compound of two trapezohedra (duals) ===
The duals of the prismatic compound of antiprisms are compounds of [[trapezohedra]]:

|- align=center
|[[File:Compound_two_cubes.png|160px]]<BR>Two cubes<BR>(trigonal trapezohedra)
|}

== Compound of three antiprisms==
For compounds of three digonal antiprisms, they are rotated 60 degrees, while three triangular antiprisms are rotated 40 degrees.
